docs.title: XR Rollout Controller
docs.text:
The controller rolls a fleet of Crossplane v2 composite resources (XRs) onto a new CompositionRevision in a fixed order: canary, soak, environment gate, then batched waves.

It governs XRs whose compositionUpdatePolicy is Manual. The only field it writes is spec.crossplane.compositionRevisionRef. Automatic XRs keep moving on their own and are counted as unmanaged.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Watch a cluster-scoped CompositionRollout and new CompositionRevision objects for the compositions it names.
  2. Canary a frozen subset (label, count, or percent) and patch those XRs first.
  3. Soak until the canaries hold Ready=True and Synced=True for the configured duration.
  4. Gate promotion with the policy for this cluster's --environment (AutoPromote or ManualApproval).
  5. Wave the remainder in bounded batches. A failure pauses the rollout. Nothing is rolled back.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
Install Public GHCR image and OCI Helm chart.

CRD CompositionRollout spec, status, and a sample manifest.

Canary and promotion Selection, soak, waves, and pause.

Environment gate One manifest, per-cluster --environment.

Triggers Start, Approve, Resume, and Abort.

Architecture Runtime, rollout flow, and the Approve sequence.

Releases Image, chart, and how a tag becomes a docs version.

Contributing Local mkdocs build and tests.

The longer design note stays in the repository: docs/xr-rollout-controller-plan.md.

docs.title: Site features
docs.text:
• Search — Material’s built-in client-side search. Use the search box in the header.
  • Versions — published with mike. Use the version selector in the header.
Version / alias Meaning latest Docs for the newest stable SemVer tag (default after the first release). Pre-releases do not move this alias. 1.2.3 Immutable docs for stable tag v1.2.3 (the leading v is removed) 1.2.3-rc.1 Docs for a pre-release tag such as v1.2.3-rc.1. latest stays on the last stable version. dev Docs from the tip of main (may change between releases)

Expected URL: https://kanzifucius.github.io/xr-rollout-controller/.

docs.title: Canary and promotion
docs.text:
Each composition on a CompositionRollout runs its own state machine.

Idle → Canarying → Soaking → AwaitingApproval or Promoting → Completed → Idle
                 ↘ Paused ← Soaking / Promoting
                   Resume returns to the phase that paused
                   Abort → Aborted → Idle (no rollback)

autoStart: true (the default) enters Canarying when a newer revision appears. onNewRevision: Restart drops an in-flight target and starts again on the newest revision. Queue finishes the current rollout first.

docs.title: Canary selection
docs.text:
spec.canary.strategy is one of:

Strategy Behaviour LabelSelector The XRs that match canary.labelSelector are the canary set. An empty match pauses with CanarySetEmpty. Count A fixed number of XRs. Percent A percentage of the fleet, rounded up, minimum 1.

Count and Percent order candidates by a hash of the XR UID, with namespace and name as the tie-break, so the same XRs are chosen across restarts. preferredNamespaces draws from those namespaces first, in list order, and is ignored for LabelSelector. Those two strategies do not read canary.labelSelector.

The chosen set is stored in status.rollouts[].canary.selected when canarying starts and is not recomputed for that rollout. A deleted canary shrinks the set. If the set becomes empty during soak, the rollout pauses.

docs.title: LabelSelector strategy
docs.text:
canary.labelSelector is used only when canary.strategy is LabelSelector. It is the same standard selector as xrSelector.labelSelector: matchLabels and matchExpressions are ANDed, and the operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.

The governed XRs that match become the canary set. preferredNamespaces is ignored. Leaving labelSelector unset, or setting an empty selector, matches every governed XR. A selector that matches nobody pauses the rollout with CanarySetEmpty.

canary:
  strategy: LabelSelector
  labelSelector:
    matchExpressions:
      - key: rollout.example.org/canary
        operator: In
        values: ["true"]

A manifest that sets both the fleet selector and this canary selector is in Fleet and canary together.

Canaries are patched with server-side apply, field manager xr-rollout-controller, changing only spec.crossplane.compositionRevisionRef.name. Crossplane's own field manager on that field is taken so a Manual rollout can proceed. A conflict with any other manager pauses with PatchFailed unless the Deployment sets --force-ownership.

docs.title: Soak
docs.text:
spec.soak.duration (default 30m) is how long every canary must hold Ready=True and Synced=True. Health means the conditions are currently True and their lastTransitionTime is at or before the soak start, so a flip to False during the window fails that XR even if it recovers.

maxUnhealthy (default 0) is how many unhealthy canaries are tolerated. stabilisationTimeout (default 30m) bounds how long the controller waits for canaries to become healthy the first time. Exceeding either pauses the rollout. Already-updated XRs stay on the new revision.

docs.title: Waves
docs.text:
After the gate, the remainder moves in waves. waves.batchSize is an integer or a percentage string such as "10%". maxConcurrentUpdates (default 20) caps in-flight patches. waveSoak (default 5m) is the health hold between waves, with its own maxUnhealthy (default 0).

A failed wave pauses with WaveUnhealthy. When every wave is healthy the phase becomes Completed, then Idle.

docs.title: Pause
docs.text:
While Paused, the controller writes no further revision refs for that composition. spec.suspend: true pauses everything with reason Suspended and ignores triggers until it is cleared.

There is no automatic rollback. Triggers covers Resume and Abort. The diagram of this path is Rollout flow.

docs.title: CompositionRollout
docs.text:
CompositionRollout is a cluster-scoped custom resource (rollouts.platform.example.org/v1alpha1). The short name is xrollout. One object covers a team's compositions. Each composition has its own revision stream and its own phase.

XRs are in scope when spec.crossplane.compositionRef.name matches a listed composition and compositionUpdatePolicy is Manual. An optional xrSelector narrows that set by namespace or labels.

docs.title: Spec
docs.text:
Field Role compositions Composition names to govern. At least one. Optional xrSelector narrows the fleet. suspend Pauses every in-flight rollout and ignores new revisions until cleared. autoStart Start a rollout when a newer revision appears. Default true. onNewRevision Restart (default) abandons the current target for a newer revision. Queue finishes the current rollout first. canary How the first subset is chosen. See Canary and promotion. soak How long canaries must stay healthy. promotion Per-environment policy after soak. See Environment gate. waves Batch size, concurrency, and the pause between waves. triggers Manual Start, Approve, Resume, and Abort. See Triggers.

The controller does not write compositionUpdatePolicy, compositionRef, labels, or any schema field on the XR. Pinning XRs to Manual is done by the XR author or by the XRD's defaultCompositionUpdatePolicy.

docs.title: Label selectors
docs.text: compositions[].xrSelector.labelSelector and canary.labelSelector are both a standard Kubernetes label selector. matchLabels and matchExpressions are ANDed. Each matchLabels entry is an In match on that single value. matchExpressions[].operator is In, NotIn, Exists, or DoesNotExist. In and NotIn take a non-empty values list. Exists and DoesNotExist take an empty one.

docs.title: Which XRs a composition governs
docs.text:
xrSelector is optional and sits on top of the composition ref. A Manual XR is in that composition's fleet only when:

  • spec.crossplane.compositionRef.name equals compositions[].name
  • compositionUpdatePolicy is Manual
  • xrSelector.namespaces, when set, includes the XR's namespace
  • xrSelector.labelSelector, when set, matches the XR's labels

namespaces is the other optional narrow. Names in the list are alternatives. The label selector is applied as well, and both have to match. Omit xrSelector, or omit one of its fields, and that narrow is not applied. A cluster-scoped XR has an empty namespace, so a namespaces list leaves it out.

compositions:
  - name: platformdb.example.org
    xrSelector:
      namespaces: [payments-prod]
      labelSelector:
        matchLabels:
          team: payments
        matchExpressions:
          - key: rollout.example.org/skip
            operator: DoesNotExist

That keeps Manual platformdb.example.org XRs in payments-prod with team=payments and without rollout.example.org/skip.

docs.title: Fleet and canary together
docs.text:
canary.labelSelector does not change the fleet. It chooses the canary set, and only when canary.strategy is LabelSelector. The strategy is documented in LabelSelector strategy.

apiVersion: rollouts.platform.example.org/v1alpha1
kind: CompositionRollout
metadata:
  name: team-payments
spec:
  compositions:
    - name: platformdb.example.org
      xrSelector:
        namespaces: [payments-dev, payments-prod]
        labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            team: payments
          matchExpressions:
            - key: env
              operator: In
              values: [dev, prod]
  canary:
    strategy: LabelSelector
    labelSelector:
      matchLabels:
        rollout.example.org/canary: "true"
  soak:
    duration: 30m
  promotion:
    defaultPolicy: ManualApproval
  waves:
    batchSize: "10%"

The fleet is Manual platformdb.example.org XRs in payments-dev or payments-prod, with team=payments and env of dev or prod. The canary set is those XRs that also have rollout.example.org/canary=true. If none do, the rollout pauses with CanarySetEmpty.

docs.title: Sample
docs.text:
apiVersion: rollouts.platform.example.org/v1alpha1
kind: CompositionRollout
metadata:
  name: team-payments
spec:
  compositions:
    - name: platformdb.example.org
    - name: platformcache.example.org
      xrSelector:
        namespaces: [payments-dev, payments-prod]
  autoStart: true
  onNewRevision: Restart
  canary:
    strategy: Percent
    percent: 5
    preferredNamespaces: [payments-dev]
  soak:
    duration: 1h
    maxUnhealthy: 0
    stabilisationTimeout: 30m
  promotion:
    defaultPolicy: ManualApproval
    environments:
      dev: AutoPromote
      test: AutoPromote
      acceptance: ManualApproval
      prod: ManualApproval
  waves:
    batchSize: "10%"
    maxConcurrentUpdates: 25
    waveSoak: 10m

The repository sample is config/samples/rollouts_v1alpha1_compositionrollout.yaml.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Top-level conditions aggregate every composition: Progressing, AwaitingApproval, Paused, and Succeeded.

status.rollouts[] is one entry per composition:

Field Role phase Idle, Canarying, Soaking, AwaitingApproval, Promoting, Paused, Completed, Aborted targetRevision CompositionRevision name and spec.revision number being rolled out totalXRs, updatedXRs, healthyXRs, unmanagedXRs Fleet accounting. Unmanaged includes Automatic XRs. canary.selected Frozen canary members (namespace / name) wave Current wave, total waves, and when the wave soak ends pauseReason Machine-readable reason while Paused acknowledgedTriggers Triggers already consumed, so each entry acts once

kubectl get compositionrollouts prints the first composition's phase.

Two CompositionRollout objects must not claim the same composition. The example admission policy rejects the overlap, and the controller still pauses both if admission is bypassed.

docs.title: Environment gate
docs.text:
The same CompositionRollout manifest can be synced to every cluster. Each controller knows its own environment from the process flag --environment (Helm value environment, default dev).

After soak, the controller looks up spec.promotion.environments[<flag>]:

Policy After a healthy soak AutoPromote Enter Promoting and start waves. ManualApproval Enter AwaitingApproval and wait for an Approve trigger bound to this revision.

If the flag's name is missing from the map, defaultPolicy applies. That field defaults to ManualApproval, so an unknown environment waits for a human.

promotion:
  defaultPolicy: ManualApproval
  environments:
    dev: AutoPromote
    test: AutoPromote
    acceptance: ManualApproval
    prod: ManualApproval

A cluster installed with --set environment=prod waits. A cluster installed with --set environment=dev promotes on its own. The manifest does not change.

AwaitingApproval is also a status condition on the CompositionRollout, so a release process can watch one object instead of the whole fleet.

The approval itself is a spec.triggers entry, not an annotation. See Triggers.

Cross-cluster order is a different mechanism from spec.promotion.environments. The environment map still decides AutoPromote or ManualApproval inside the cluster after soak. See Promotion across clusters.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Releases publish a multi-arch controller image and a Helm chart to GHCR. Both packages are public: pull and install them without a registry login or an image pull secret.

Chart --version is SemVer without a leading v. Image tags keep v. A pre-release chart keeps the suffix, for example 1.2.3-rc.1.

helm install xr-rollout-controller \
  oci://ghcr.io/kanzifucius/charts/xr-rollout-controller \
  --version 1.2.3 \
  --namespace xr-rollout-controller-system \
  --create-namespace \
  --set environment=dev

Replace 1.2.3 with the chart version (the git tag with the leading v removed). The chart installs the CompositionRollout CRD, the controller Deployment, RBAC, a metrics Service, and the example ValidatingAdmissionPolicy.

docs.title: Image
docs.text:
Images are built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.

Tag Published when vX.Y.Z A stable semver tag is pushed, including optional +build metadata. The image is that tag only. vX.Y.Z-<pre> A pre-release tag such as v1.2.3-rc.1 or v1.2.3-alpha.1 is pushed. The image is that tag only. latest is left unchanged. <short-sha> A commit is pushed to main (7-character SHA) latest A commit is pushed to main 
docker pull ghcr.io/kanzifucius/xr-rollout-controller:latest

The image reference inside a published chart is ghcr.io/kanzifucius/xr-rollout-controller:vX.Y.Z.

Private forks still need a token with read:packages and an image pull secret. Pass it with --set imagePullSecrets[0].name=ghcr.

docs.title: Chart values
docs.text:
Value Default Purpose image.repository ghcr.io/kanzifucius/xr-rollout-controller Controller image repository image.tag chart appVersion Image tag. Release charts set appVersion to the git tag, for example v1.2.3 environment dev Passed as --environment forceOwnership false Force server-side apply ownership of the revision ref metricsAggregateOnly false Drop per-composition Prometheus labels resources 10m/64Mi request, 500m/128Mi limit Container resources metrics.service.enabled true Metrics Service on port 8443 metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled false Prometheus Operator ServiceMonitor admissionPolicy.enabled true Example ValidatingAdmissionPolicy 
helm upgrade --install xr-rollout-controller \
  oci://ghcr.io/kanzifucius/charts/xr-rollout-controller \
  --version 1.2.3 \
  --namespace xr-rollout-controller-system \
  --set environment=prod

Approve and Resume triggers are rejected unless the caller is in the group rollouts.platform.example.org:release-managers. Set admissionPolicy.enabled=false to skip that policy.

XR access is aggregated from ClusterRoles labelled rollouts.platform.example.org/aggregate-to-rollout-controller=true. The chart binds that aggregate ClusterRole to the controller ServiceAccount. aggregationRule is a top-level field on the ClusterRole.

Helm installs CRDs from crds/ on the first install and does not upgrade them. After a chart upgrade, apply the compositionrollouts.crd.yaml asset from the GitHub Release.

docs.title: Release manifests
docs.text:
Each GitHub Release also attaches install.yaml and compositionrollouts.crd.yaml. install.yaml includes the CRDs, RBAC, and the controller Deployment pinned to the release image. It does not set --environment (the binary default is dev) and it does not include the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy. Use the Helm chart when you need the environment flag and the policy.

install.yaml is built from config/. In that tree, aggregationRule on the XR ClusterRole is nested under metadata, which the API server rejects. The Helm chart places aggregationRule at the top level. Prefer the chart until that manifest is corrected.

gh release download v1.2.3 --repo kanzifucius/xr-rollout-controller --pattern install.yaml
kubectl apply -f install.yaml

Cutting a tag publishes the image, the chart, the GitHub Release, and a docs version together. See Releases.

docs.title: Promotion across clusters
docs.text:
The promoter runs in the management cluster. Each spoke still runs its own rollout controller, and that controller still rolls only that cluster's composite resources (XRs). The promoter does not patch an XR. It opens the next cluster's gate by appending one Start trigger.

One management install is given kubeconfigs for dev, test, acc, and prod. Each kubeconfig is a Secret in the release namespace:

apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: dev
  namespace: xr-rollout
  labels:
    sigs.k8s.io/multicluster-runtime-kubeconfig: "true"
type: Opaque
data:
  kubeconfig: <base64 kubeconfig>

The Secret name is the cluster name. The data key is kubeconfig. Repeat the Secret for test, acc, and prod. The chart does not create these Secrets.

The order is not the order the Secrets were created. It is PromotionPipeline.spec.clusters, which the chart renders from promoter.clusters (default dev, test, acc, prod). A pipeline lists 2 to 32 clusters. Each name is unique and at most 253 characters, the same limit as a Secret name. Enable the promoter with --set promoter.enabled=true and, on that management install, --set rollout.enabled=false. A spoke install does the opposite: the rollout controller stays on, and the promoter stays off.

dev keeps autoStart: true. test, acc, and prod set autoStart: false. The promoter does not change that field. If a later cluster leaves autoStart: true, that cluster can start a revision before the previous one finishes. The promoter will not append a Start that the spoke would acknowledge as Stale. It records that the revision has already started, and it still waits for that cluster to finish before opening the cluster after it.

A hop writes one trigger:

Field Value action Start revision the completed CompositionRevision name actor xr-rollout-promoter

The field manager is xr-rollout-promoter. Paused or Aborted on the lower cluster leaves the next cluster unstarted. Abort does not roll XRs back.

The spoke --environment value is still the in-cluster policy key (acceptance in the samples). It is not required to equal the cluster name acc.

Apply spoke CompositionRollout objects with server-side apply, so GitOps does not own the promoter's trigger key. spec.triggers is a map keyed by composition, action, and revision. The controller acknowledges a trigger in status. It does not delete it.

On each spoke, bind the kubeconfig identity to the ClusterRole in config/rbac/promoter_remote_role.yaml (also packaged at charts/xr-rollout-controller/files/promoter-remote-rbac.yaml). Do not reuse the XR aggregation role. That remote role can read rollout status and patch spec.triggers. It cannot write status, and it cannot touch XRs.

The management process reaches each cluster with the multicluster-runtime client library. Nothing else from that SIG has to be installed on the spokes.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
A maintainer cuts a release by pushing an annotated semver tag. Do not create the GitHub Release in the UI first; the Release workflow creates it.

git checkout main && git pull
git tag -a v1.2.3 -m "v1.2.3"
git push origin v1.2.3

A pre-release uses the same flow:

git tag -a v1.2.3-rc.1 -m "v1.2.3-rc.1"
git push origin v1.2.3-rc.1

The tag must match vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, with an optional pre-release suffix and optional build metadata (v1.2.3-rc.1, v1.2.3-alpha.1, v1.2.3-rc.1+exp.1). Build metadata on its own (v1.2.3+sha) is still a stable release. A hyphen only inside the build metadata does not make a pre-release.

Image registries reject + in a tag. Publish a pre-release you want to pull without build metadata (v1.2.3-rc.1). When the git tag includes +build, the chart version and the docs version keep that suffix.

docs.title: What the tag publishes
docs.text:
Two workflows run on that push. Release publishes the artefacts. docs publishes the site. They do not call each other. Both ask hack/release-tag.sh whether the tag is stable or a pre-release.

Artefact Where Name Controller image ghcr.io/kanzifucius/xr-rollout-controller the git tag. The latest image tag is published from main only. Helm chart oci://ghcr.io/kanzifucius/charts/xr-rollout-controller tag without v (1.2.3 or 1.2.3-rc.1). appVersion is the git tag. A pre-release stays on that version. It is not copied onto a stable version or latest. GitHub Release this repository install.yaml and compositionrollouts.crd.yaml, with generated notes. A pre-release is created with --prerelease and --latest=false. Docs version GitHub Pages (mike tree on gh-pages) tag without v. Stable tags also move the latest alias. Pre-releases leave latest on the last stable version.

Pushes to main publish the image as the short SHA and as latest. They do not push a Helm chart. They do publish docs version dev.

docs.title: How a release shows up in the docs
docs.text:
The site is built with Material for MkDocs and deployed with mike onto the gh-pages branch. GitHub Pages serves that branch (folder /). There is no custom domain. The site URL is https://kanzifucius.github.io/xr-rollout-controller/.

Push mike version Alias main dev dev is the default only until the first release sets one tag v1.2.3 1.2.3 latest is updated, and latest becomes the default tag v1.2.3+sha 1.2.3+sha latest is updated (build metadata is not a pre-release) tag v1.3.0-rc.1 1.3.0-rc.1 latest stays on the last stable version tag v1.3.0-alpha.1 1.3.0-alpha.1 latest stays on the last stable version

After v1.2.3 is pushed, the version dropdown lists 1.2.3 and latest points at those pages. The next stable tag moves latest. A later pre-release publishes its own version beside that alias. Older versions stay addressable, for example /1.2.3/ beside /latest/, /1.3.0-rc.1/, and /dev/.

The first successful docs deploy on main creates gh-pages. Pages must be set once to Deploy from a branch, branch gh-pages, folder / (root). The workflow does not use the github-pages environment: that environment only allows deployments from gh-pages, and this job runs on main.

docs.title: Triggers
docs.text:
spec.triggers is the manual control surface. The controller never deletes or edits spec (GitOps would fight that). It records consumption on status.rollouts[].acknowledgedTriggers. A trigger already acknowledged for the same composition, action, and revision is a no-op.

Each entry names the composition, the action, an optional revision, and an optional actor string for audit. An omitted Start revision is stored as an empty string. That empty string is the map key for latest.

Action When it applies Revision Start Phase is Idle. Begins canarying the latest revision, or the named revision when it is that latest revision. Optional. An explicit name must be the latest revision. Approve Phase is AwaitingApproval. Enters Promoting. Required, and must equal the target revision. Resume Phase is Paused. Returns to the phase stored in phaseBeforePause (or Canarying if that is empty) and clears the pause reason. Required, and must equal the target revision. Abort Phase is AwaitingApproval or Paused. Moves to Aborted, then Idle. Required, and must equal the target revision.

A promoter may append Start for one revision. The controller still only acknowledges that entry. A Stale acknowledgement is not retried for that revision.

A trigger that does not match the phase or revision is acknowledged with outcome Stale and does not change the phase. autoStart will not immediately start a rollout for a revision that was aborted. A later Start can run that revision again from Canarying.

Abort does not revert XRs. Canaries already on the new revision stay there. The rest stay on the old one until a later rollout moves them.

spec:
  triggers:
    - composition: platformdb.example.org
      action: Approve
      revision: platformdb.example.org-9f8a2c1
      actor: ricardo@example.org

docs.title: Admission
docs.text:
The chart's ValidatingAdmissionPolicy allows Start and Abort for any caller who can update the object. Approve and Resume require the group rollouts.platform.example.org:release-managers. Approve, Resume, and Abort must set revision.

Disable the policy with --set admissionPolicy.enabled=false only when another control covers that group.

The message order for a successful Approve is Approve sequence.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: The controller is one manager process. It watches CompositionRollout, CompositionRevision, and the composite resource types those compositions produce, then patches Manual XRs onto a target revision.

docs.title: Diagrams
docs.text:
Interactive Archify HTML is embedded on each caption page. Open the standalone file for a full browser tab.

Diagram Page Standalone HTML Runtime Runtime diagram xr-rollout-runtime.html Canary, soak, and promotion Rollout flow rollout-flow.html Approve trigger Approve sequence approve-sequence.html

docs.title: What the pages leave in prose
docs.text:
• The CRD lists every spec and status field.
  • Canary and promotion covers selection, soak, and waves.
  • Triggers covers Start, Resume, and Abort as well as Approve.

The design note in git is docs/xr-rollout-controller-plan.md.

docs.title: Runtime diagram
docs.text:
How an install reaches the reconciler, how a new CompositionRevision wakes it, and the single field written on Manual XRs.

Operator installs the public OCI chart; the manager reconciles each composition; revisions enqueue on create; server-side apply writes compositionRevisionRef; admission guards Approve and Resume on the rollout object. Open standalone HTML.

The Helm values and image tags are in Install.

docs.title: Approve sequence
docs.text:
A release manager adds an Approve trigger. Admission checks the group, the reconciler asks the state machine, and a matching revision moves the composition to Promoting.

Approve is admitted for rollouts.platform.example.org:release-managers, applied only in AwaitingApproval for the target revision, then acknowledged on status. Open standalone HTML.

Start, Resume, and Abort use the same trigger list. See Triggers.

docs.title: Rollout flow
docs.text:
One composition, from a new revision through canary, soak, the environment gate, and waves. The pause branch is the unhealthy soak. Canary and wave failures pause the same way; Resume and Abort are described beside the diagram.

autoStart or Start freezes a canary and patches it; a held health window opens the environment gate; AutoPromote or Approve starts waves; Completed returns to Idle. Open standalone HTML.

Field-level behaviour: Canary and promotion and Environment gate.
